h2: Magnetic particle testing in New England: one method, several boiler jurisdictions
html:
Magnetic particle testing in New England: one method, several boiler jurisdictions

Magnetic particle testing in New England covers the same ferromagnetic welds, forgings and castings in every state, but the paperwork changes at each state line. Massachusetts, Connecticut, Maine, New Hampshire and Rhode Island each place boiler and pressure vessel oversight with a different agency, so MT on a repair is planned around whoever holds the equipment record. Atlantis mobilises MT crews to sites across the region.

Where the jurisdiction sits, state by state:

  • Massachusetts: rules set by the Board of Boiler Rules in 522 CMR, with state District Engineering Inspectors performing initial inspections.
  • Maine: the Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation, as listed in the National Board's member directory.
  • New Hampshire: the Department of Labor.
  • Rhode Island: the Department of Labor and Training, Division of Occupational Safety.
  • Connecticut: its own state boiler program; the current jurisdictional contact for a given vessel is confirmed when the job is quoted.

MT on repairs. Massachusetts adopts the 2021 National Board Inspection Code through 522 CMR 15.00, and the NBIC governs repairs and alterations to boilers and pressure vessels in service. On carbon-steel pressure parts, MT is the usual surface examination of the excavation before welding and of the finished repair. The inspector who accepts the repair is the jurisdiction's or the Authorized Inspection Agency's, never the NDT contractor, so the MT report has to name the procedure, technique, equipment and acceptance standard clearly enough for that inspector to rely on it.

When radiography joins the scope. All six New England states are NRC Agreement States, so radiography of a repair weld is licensed by the state's own radiation program rather than by the NRC. In Massachusetts that is the Radiation Control Division of the Department of Public Health, and its industrial radiography rules in 105 CMR 120.300 provide for state certification of industrial radiographers working in the Commonwealth. The radiography arrangements and the licence holder are confirmed for each job before any source is brought to site.

Editions across state lines. Each state adopts the codes it enforces by regulation, and adoption dates do not move in step. A contractor working the whole region should write MT procedures that state which ASME Section V edition and which NBIC edition they follow, and check those against the jurisdiction holding the equipment before the job, rather than assuming the Massachusetts adoption carries over the border.

Winter MT. Much New England field work happens in cold, damp conditions. Water-based baths can freeze and oil carriers thicken, so particle concentration is checked by settling test at the working temperature, and fluorescent work needs a properly darkened enclosure that an exposed winter site rarely provides without planning. Surface moisture and ice are removed before magnetisation, because particles cannot form an indication on a wet film over a crack.

The magnetic particle testing service describes wet, dry and fluorescent techniques, US weld inspection services covers fabrication and repair welds, and procedure development helps New England shops whose MT procedures need rewriting to the current NBIC and ASME editions. Massachusetts firms needing Level III support can use NDT consulting in Massachusetts. To scope MT anywhere in New England, tell us the state, asset and code.
